amendments.normalized_body: All five fixture functions (breeding_success_state, thermal_scenario_state, chemistry_stress_state, chloride_test_base_state, crash_mode_state) manually override DIC, alkalinity, and bicarbonate_mg_total after calling WaterState::default_for_volume_l, but never re-solve carbonate equilibrium before calling reseed_stability_tracker(). This leaves state.water.ph stale (derived from the default DIC=20/alk=1.5 chemistry, roughly pH 7.3) while the actual overridden chemistry (e.g., DIC=5/alk=12 in breeding_success_state) would resolve to a significantly different pH (likely >8.5). On the first hourly tick, apply_hourly_chemistry_terms calls resolve_carbonate_state, correcting pH — but the stability tracker's prev_ph still holds the stale value, causing a false instability signal from the pH discontinuity. Fix: insert a resolve_carbonate_state(&mut state.water, vol) call after setting custom DIC/alkalinity/bicarbonate and before reseed_stability_tracker() in each fixture function. This ensures the initial state is internally consistent and the stability tracker baseline matches the actual chemistry.

The patch does not implement the bead it is supposed to close. The only new coverage is a nitrification/alkalinity suite in crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1, and the runtime changes are limited to alkalinity bookkeeping/tracing around the nitrogen cycle in crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:229, crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:12, and crates/tank_core/src/systems/water_change.rs:131. None of the requested shrimp scenario tests, the 1000+ hour breeding run, the per-tick shrimp/water trace dumps, or the e2e summary runner/report are present, so the acceptance criteria for tanksim-6e5.6.6 are still unmet.

The new alkalinity diagnostics still print the wrong unit in the detailed failure paths. assert_budget_balanced switches the headline to meq, but the per-system lines are still hard-coded to mg at crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:474, and assert_per_tick_balanced still hard-codes mg at crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:496 and crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:502. If an alkalinity assertion fails, the report will mix meq and mg in the same message and mislead anyone trying to calibrate or debug the failure.
